newsitem.title: USA: AEP says still no restart for 1,300 MW Ohio plant.
newsitem.headline: AEP says still no restart for 1,300 MW Ohio plant.

text.p: American Electric Power Co (AEP) said it has not yet set a restart date for the 1,300 megawatt (MW) Gavin coal-fired power unit 2 in Cheshire, Ohio, after a lightning strike forced its shutdown.
"We have no (restart) estimate, we are still determining what repairs are necessary," an AEP spokesman said Wednesday.
The Gavin 2 unit was shut one week ago when lightning struck a main transformer at the unit and caused a fire.
AEP has postponed regular maintenance at other electricity generation units to make up for supply lost from Gavin unit 2.
The damaged transformer "steps up", or raises the voltage level from 26,000 volts from Gavin unit 2 for transmission across a 765,000 volt transmission line.
AEP has a total generating capacity of 24,700 MW.
